cases.question: My overlap fractions are high but both correlation measures are negative. Can I report strong interaction, or how can these results coexist?
review_criteria: Distinguish threshold occupancy from intensity covariation
cases.answer: High Manders overlap fractions indicate that most of the signal from Marker A is within the threshold of Marker B, and vice versa [measurements]. These results can coexist if both proteins occupy the same general region but exhibit opposing intensity patterns, such as one being highly concentrated in a specific sub-compartment while the other is excluded or diffuse in that same area [methods]. Conventional microscopy cannot establish molecular binding or causality from these colocalization metrics [interpretation]. Advice: You should inspect the background and threshold settings, as zero thresholds can result in high overlap fractions from pervasive diffuse signal that does not represent specific interaction [interpretation].
